title: Baby Dodds as a drummer
summary: Moore and Dodds drank and talked drums; Dodds had his own style with rim work and press rolls and little cymbal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What about the drummer Baby Dodds, Freddie? Did you have much opportunity to talk with him, to hang around him? Did you get along all right with him?

Yes. We used to get together sometime ago in the bar, and have a few drinks, started talking about different drummers. His whole mind was set on me... He liked my drumming. And I liked his drumming. But Baby Dodds had a big name. When I come to New York in 1928, you'd hear a lot of talk about Baby Dodds, which...
He had been well established by then.

I think he was in New York by that time. He had a little difficulty... And quite there was quite a few drummers, some White boys, who wanted to play like him. But Baby Dodds had his own thing going, his own style, you know. He'd play on the rim of the drums and press rolls; he'd do a lot of press-rolling on the snare drum. You'd not hear too much cymbal work.
